chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad al-Ashʿarī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir, from ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from Faḍālah, from Abān, from al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbd al-Malik or Ibn Abī Yaʿfūr, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, that he said:

Regarding a man who performs salat (prayer) but did not begin with the takbir, does the takbir of rukūʿ suffice for him? He said: No. Rather, he must repeat his salat (prayer) if he is certain that he did not say the takbir.

key_terms.بِالتَّكْبِيرِ: with the opening takbir that begins the prayer
key_terms.تَكْبِيرَةُ الرُّكُوعِ: the takbir uttered when going into rukūʿ
key_terms.تُجْزِيهِ: suffices for him or fulfills the requirement
key_terms.حَفِظَ: he is certain or preserves awareness

ai.seo_question: Does the takbir of rukūʿ count if someone forgot Takbīrat al-Iftitāḥ in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning one who omitted Takbīrat al-Iftitāḥ at the start of salat (prayer). It states that the takbir said for rukūʿ does not compensate for the opening takbir, and the prayer must be repeated when the omission is known with certainty.
